title: Kingdom
description: kingdom.json at the root of a kingdom directory (one machine, one user, one kingdom). The kingdom directory is chosen with `elvaria init --kingdom <dir>` and lives outside the Elvaria repo. Holds the owner's settings: tribes (one per signed-in account, each run by an adapter), mana cap and king's reserve, circuit breakers, schedules, dispatch policy, bell channels, tunnel, theme and UI mode. `elvaria doctor` fills `tribes[].tool`.
$comment: Generated by `pnpm schemas` from the zod source in packages/domain/src/schema (ADR 0003): change the zod source, never this file. Paths inside kingdom files are relative to the kingdom directory with '/' separators; the only absolute paths are territory.path and paths.treasury (implementation-plan §2.1). Not expressible here: tz must be a time zone Intl knows.

name.description: Kingdom name chosen by the owner; rendered with `.elv-name` (24ch).

tz.description: IANA time zone of the machine (e.g. Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh). Event files are named by local day; recording tz keeps replays consistent.

locale.description: Language of everything the owner reads: handover letters, verdict notes, blocked questions, chronicle, bell, UI.

treasury.description: Treasury file (secrets), always outside the kingdom, e.g. ~/.elvaria/treasury.json resolved to an absolute path.

tribes.description: Tribes (product plan 0.6, tribe contract): one entry per account the owner signs in to on this machine. Adding a tribe = an adapter (built in, or a file adapters/<name>.mjs in the kingdom) + a look (the owner's choice, the theme's pinned entry, or one drawn from the theme's look pool by the id, PS-24) + the owner's own login; the core and existing characters do not change. `elvaria init` writes claude (claude_code) and gemini (antigravity). The Steward reads each adapter's capabilities at start and narrows what that tribe may take (implementation-plan §3.14). Ids are unique (zod).

programs.description: Programs outside Node that Elvaria runs, each pinned like a tribe CLI.

graphify.description: graphify (the Python package graphifyy), found and pinned by `elvaria doctor --pin` when a territory has code_graph on: the Steward builds the code graphs with it, with no model and a fixed env (ADR 0029). Doctor warns when it is missing or its version differs; a missing graphify never stops a quest.

mana.$comment: Intake threshold per pool = min(cap_pct, 100 - king_reserve_pct). The world never takes new quests at or above it; a warning fires warn_margin_pct points earlier.

reassign_after_hours.description: If set, a quest in paused_mana longer than this may be reassigned to another character by rule. null = never (principle 6 keeps the assignee).

high.description: Ranks from high_rank_from up, and territories with an exclusive e2e check.

mana_multiplier.description: quest.budget.max_tokens = estimate.tokens x mana_multiplier, never below the rank's share of context_budget_tokens x mana_multiplier.

subagent_max_minutes.description: Measured only (hook SubagentStart/Stop); overrun emits agent.subagent.overrun and counts against the parent quest.

subagent_max_turns.description: The enforceable apprentice breaker: maxTurns of the `apprentice` agent definition.

context_budget_tokens.description: The Chancellor splits work so one quest fits one context (principle 13).

verifier_tokens_multiplier.description: A judge's session may spend this many times quest.budget.max_tokens before the token breaker stops it: it reads the whole diff and runs the checks again. The assignee's sessions keep quest.budget.max_tokens.

schedule.$comment: Scheduled jobs run inside the Steward (no cron, Task Scheduler or launchd). The digest (PS-03) and the triage (PS-03b) have a runner and are on by default; chronicle, temple and patrol have none yet, so they default to disabled.

triage.description: The Chancellor's triage of the memos waiting (PS-03b): at `at`, before the digest, one model call for the batch of memos sent to the Chancellor that nobody has decided or sent up yet, run outside the Steward's tick once no session of the Chancellor's tribe runs; none when no memo waits. Its result is inbox commands only, applied without the owner within `delegation`.

digest.description: The daily digest (PS-03): at `at` the Steward writes digest/YYYY-MM-DD.md, everything that waits for the owner in two groups (must decide for the work to go on, can wait), each item with advice and its CLI command, and rings the bell once. No model, no mana; once a day, whatever the clock does.

verifier_same_family.description: When no verifier of another model family is free: different_model requires a different model slug; machine_only lets the Steward issue a machine verdict (never pass with a failing check).

resume_after_mana.description: Revive with `--resume <session>` instead of a fresh session built from handover.md. Off by default (principle 13, ADR 0017).

resume_after_answer_minutes.description: When the owner answers a character's question within this many minutes of blocked.asked_at and the tribe's adapter can resume, the same CLI session goes on (`--resume`); later, or null, a fresh session starts from handover.md with the answer (ADR 0017).

max_background.description: How many pieces of machine work the Steward runs outside its tick at once, kingdom-wide: a submitted quest's checks (or its trial in a scratch plot) and a script-tier quest's script. The next waits for a later tick. Cautious until measured.

council.description: When the Chancellor sends work through the council (PS-06, product plan 0.8 §14): a brief with every question for the owner asked once, a plan quest of a mage that waits for the owner's seal, a review of the plan, then the sub-quests. A reply of smaller work goes straight to drafts as before; a reply of larger work without that plan and brief is returned to the Chancellor once.

from_rank.description: Work with a session draft of this rank or above goes through the council.

from_areas.description: Work whose session drafts carry at least this many tags over at least this many areas goes through the council too. An area is a territory, or within one the globs of scope_paths that meet (shared_paths aside); a draft without a scope covers its whole territory.

delegation.description: Delegation (PS-03b, product plan 0.8 §14): which of the memos the Chancellor triages (`kingdom.schedule.triage`, `elvaria triage`) the Steward applies without the owner. A memo the Chancellor merges into an open quest, makes a new quest of, or sets aside is applied when no reason of `ask` holds, and, for work, when its rank is at most max_rank and, with same_scope, its files lie in the work's scope; any other goes to the owner with the Chancellor's advice, and into the digest. The Chancellor's own choice to send a memo up always holds.

max_rank.description: The highest rank of the work the world takes in alone: the open quest a memo merges into, or the new quest made of it. Above it the memo goes to the owner.

same_scope.description: The memo's files must lie in the scope_paths of the quest that does the work, on the territory of the quest that wrote it: a merge never widens a scope, a new quest has one covering them. A memo without files, or work without a scope, then goes to the owner.

ask.description: The matters the owner keeps: a memo the Chancellor flags with one of them goes to the owner whatever its rank and scope. All five by default.

messaging.description: Messaging channel, chosen in stage 2; null until then.

abs_path.description: Absolute path with '/' separators (Windows drive or POSIX root); no backslashes in data files.

id.description: TribeId, referenced by character.tribe and class.default_tribe. The tribe's look (name, palette, crest…) is `look`, else the theme's pinned entry for this id, else drawn from the theme's look pool by it (PS-24).

adapter.description: A built-in adapter (claude_code, antigravity, gemini_cli, codex_cli) or an adapter file adapters/<name>.mjs inside the kingdom that exports createAdapter(kit) and passes the conformance suite.

tool.description: The CLI binary, filled and pinned by `elvaria doctor`. Doctor warns when the installed version differs and refuses adapter = antigravity without terms_acknowledged_at.

auth.description: login = the owner's own sign-in saved by the unmodified CLI (claude.ai, Google, ChatGPT); api_key = a key from the treasury (paid, so budget.usd_week is required; mandatory for Claude if Elvaria is shared with other people). It must be one the adapter declares in capabilities.auth (Gemini CLI: api_key only); `elvaria doctor` and `elvaria tribe check` check that, not this schema, which names no adapter (ADR 0021).

terms_acknowledged_at.description: When the owner acknowledged the provider's terms for wrapping its CLI (Antigravity: not supported on consumer plans, ADR 0018).

pools.description: Adapters with several mana pools in one account (antigravity: gemini_models on, claude_gpt_models off by default so the Gemini tribe really is the Gemini model family). Tribe state is computed per pool.

budget.description: Denominator for the `estimate` gauge source (implementation-plan §3.5): tokens of the sessions in each window, or their minutes for a tribe without usage; used for a pool and window the account reports no figure for. Each pool of the tribe is measured against it.

minutes_5h.description: Session minutes in five hours: the denominator for a tribe whose adapter reports no usage (mana_source elapsed_time, implementation-plan §3.14).

minutes_7d.description: Session minutes in seven days, as minutes_5h.

usd_week.description: Weekly spend ceiling; required when tool.auth = api_key (a paid key has no hard cap of its own).

look.description: The owner's choice of look (`elvaria tribe look`, PS-24), every part an id of the theme's look pool (tribe-looks.schema.json). Added after v1 and optional, so kingdom.json stays version 1. It wins over the theme's pinned entry; a part the pool lacks sets the whole choice aside. Absent: the theme's pinned entry for this tribe id, else a look drawn from the pool by the id. Display only: no prompt and no dispatch reads it (ADR 0025).

palette.description: Palette: the colour of the crest, the mana bar and the tint of the models.

crest.description: Crest: the icon on the banner, the portrait and the mana bar (`crest-<id>`).

figure.description: Figure: the body the characters of the tribe are built on; the class dresses it.

aura.description: Aura: how the tribe's mana shows around its characters.

frame.description: Portrait frame: the shape around a character of the tribe on the 2D screens.

name.description: The tribe's display name, the owner's words like a character's name; absent: the theme's words for its crest and palette.
